closingSelfCheck.summary: All 12 checklist items are backed by real, non-mocked machine tests (genuine two-process spawn race, real dispatched handlers via createMainRegistry, non-vacuous mutation-based wiring-detectability, live enforce-gate differential). All 9 committed red-w2c-*.mjs tests, the chain smoke, and all three registry contracts pass when run directly. I independently reproduced both the fixed crash (via a pre-fix tree checkout) and the still-open pre-existing versionless-record defect described in limitations, confirming both are substantively accurate. However, the summary/checklist overclaim in one specific respect: the 'sha256 ... across five v1 scenarios' differential-proof claim is not backed by any committed, reproducible artifact (no such hash or five-scenario run exists anywhere in the repo), and two 'defense-in-depth' assertions in the committed tests do not actually exercise the code path they claim to (Array.prototype.some short-circuits past the injected non-v1 record when a prior v1 record already satisfies) -- though the substantive fix is still independently proven true via other paths in the same test files (the v2-only/v3-only scenarios, and the read-path fail-closed classifier). The 'filed as its own task' claim for the pre-existing defect is unverifiable from repository state.
